about: Props: downloaded models placed by explicit anchors, never fitted to a footprint. A stand-in (blender/models.json) replaces a structure's outline and is fitted to it; a prop is an object that stood on the plateau, drawn where this file says and nowhere else. Nothing here is a measurement. A placement is a look choice unless its note cites a plan and says which, and the statues' grid is a placeholder that Track L's emplacements from Hoelscher replace: Props.tsx prefers the measurement keys khafre_valley_temple.statue.<n>.east/north wherever the database has them. `python scripts/props.py` fetches each source into build/props/<id>/ and pins its sha256 here; `pnpm web-assets` bakes, decimates and compresses them into apps/web/public/props/ with props/manifest.json beside them. FRAME: east, north and up are the project frame in metres (origin the Great Pyramid's base centre, +X east, +Y north, +Z up); `yaw` is a compass bearing in degrees, clockwise from north, of the direction the prop faces, and `front` says which way the source model faces before that bearing is applied. SCALE: `scale_to` is the size the prop is baked to, in metres, and always cites the size of the object itself or names itself a look choice; nothing about a prop's form or size enters data/. GROUND: the baker stands every prop's base at its own origin and sinks it by `ground_z` metres, so a consumer (Props.tsx here, Track I's scatter for the plants) places a prop at the ground and needs no further offset; props/manifest.json echoes `ground_z` and adds the measured `size`.

props.name: Seated statue of Khafre
props.author: pmanuelian (Peter Der Manuelian, Harvard Giza Project)
props.attribution: "Seated Statue of Khafre" by pmanuelian (Peter Der Manuelian, Harvard Giza Project), CC BY 4.0. A photogrammetric scan of the diorite statue found in Khafre's valley temple, Cairo JE 10062. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024; nothing about its form is changed.
props.evidence: stand-in: a scan of the statue itself, placed by hand
props.note: The one statue of the twenty-three that survived, so the same scan stands for all of them. 1.68 m is the diorite statue's own height (Cairo JE 10062), which is the object's size and not a measurement of Giza. The placements are a grid of twenty-three inside the valley temple's OSM footprint, one king in the clear middle of each bay of the colonnade the temple builder draws (5 m pitch, 1.5 m pillars, its own centroid), every one facing east toward the door: a look choice throughout, standing in until Track L enters Hoelscher's twenty-three emplacements, which Props.tsx will prefer as soon as the keys khafre_valley_temple.statue.<n>.east/north exist. The floor is the footprint's own base level, -42.18 m.

props.name: Recumbent jackal
props.author: camcolab (Cameron Colabella)
props.attribution: "Recumbent Jackal Final Model" by Cameron Colabella, CC BY 4.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024; nothing about its form is changed.
props.evidence: claim: the guardians are the design's staging for The First Time
props.note: A pair flanking the east door of each Old Kingdom temple, in the ancient state only. No record puts a jackal at any of these doors: the pair, the 2.5 m length, the 3.5 m stand-off and the 8 m between them are all look choices, and the door is taken as the midpoint of the footprint's east face, which is a look choice too. Amenhotep II's temple gets none: it is a New Kingdom building and has no place in The First Time.

props.name: Khufu's solar ship
props.author: juanbrualla (Arqueomodel3D)
props.attribution: "Khufu solar ship - EGYPT" by juanbrualla (Arqueomodel3D), CC BY 4.0. A reconstruction of the cedar ship lifted from the pit south of the Great Pyramid in 1954, not a scan of it. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: claim: the ship afloat in an open pit is the design's staging for The First Time
props.note: 43.6 m is the Khufu ship's own length as reconstructed in its museum, which is the object's size and not a measurement of Giza. It is set on the floor of the north-eastern boat pit east of the Great Pyramid, at the centroid of g1.boat_pit.north_east and 6 m below its base, which is the pit's own depth from tier3.boat_pit.depth; that the pit stood open with a ship in it is the claim, and the ship the pits held was Khufu's and lay south of the Pyramid, not here. Ancient only.
props.dropped: 2026-09-17: the only full-size Khufu ship on Sketchfab is a dense point cloud (6.2 million points, no faces: the author calls it a dense cloud test), and a point cloud is not a surface the scene can draw or the simplifier can decimate. The alternatives a search turned up are Middle Kingdom wooden tomb models with painted crews a foot long, which at 43.6 m would be a different object pretending to be this one. Kept here with its placement so that a real model drops straight in; nothing is drawn in the boat pit until one does.

props.name: Date palm
props.author: evolveduk
props.attribution: "Date Palm" by evolveduk, CC BY 4.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: claim: the Green Sahara's planting is the design's staging, the African Humid Period its reason

scatter_to.note: A look choice, not a measurement. A date palm is a bare trunk and a dozen fronds, and the fronds are what has to survive: at 2,500 each frond keeps its taper and the crown still reads as a palm from the water. The coarsest ratio level was 9,531, which at seven hundred palms was 6.7 million triangles a frame.

props.note: No placements: Track I's Vegetation.tsx scatters the plants by its own mask. 12 m is a look choice, a mature date palm's ordinary height. Poly Haven has no palm, so this one is Sketchfab's.

props.name: Desert shrub
props.author: Poly Haven
props.attribution: "shrub_02" from Poly Haven, CC0 1.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: claim: the Green Sahara's planting is the design's staging, the African Humid Period its reason

scatter_to.note: A look choice, not a measurement. A desert shrub is a mass of small leaves and never fills more than a few dozen pixels where it is scattered, so six hundred triangles is a silhouette and a little depth in it, which is all that is ever seen of one.

props.note: No placements: Track I scatters it. The pack ships four variations of the same bush side by side in one file; the first is kept, so a scatter puts one bush where it asks for one, and 1.7 m is that bush's own height. shrub_01 was fetched first and dropped after looking at it: it is not a shrub but a row of eight small seedlings spread over 2.6 m in a single mesh, with no node to cut one out of, and scattering it would have stood a row of eight wherever Track I asked for a bush.

props.name: Wild rooibos bush
props.author: Poly Haven
props.attribution: "wild_rooibos_bush" from Poly Haven, CC0 1.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: claim: the Green Sahara's planting is the design's staging, the African Humid Period its reason

scatter_to.note: A look choice, not a measurement. The rooibos bush is the smallest plant scattered and stands at 0.45 m, so it is a handful of pixels at any distance the scatter reaches; six hundred triangles is the same budget the desert shrub has, because at that size the two cost the same and differ only in colour.

props.note: No placements: Track I scatters it. A South African shrub standing in for the scrub of a wetter Sahara, which is a look choice. The pack ships five variations of the same bush side by side in one file; the middle one is kept, so a scatter puts one bush where it asks for one. 0.45 m is that bush's own height.

props.name: Island tree
props.author: Poly Haven
props.attribution: "island_tree_01" from Poly Haven, CC0 1.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: claim: the Green Sahara's planting is the design's staging, the African Humid Period its reason

scatter_to.note: A look choice, not a measurement, and it changes only how the tree is drawn and never where one stands. Three thousand triangles is what an acacia is worth at the distance it is scattered to, which is the savanna horizon: the coarsest ratio level came out at 169,160 triangles across three meshes, and seven hundred of those is 118 million triangles a frame before the shadow passes, which is why the built and ancient states drew at five frames a second (director, 2026-09-18). It is the largest budget of the four because the island tree is the largest plant and the only one whose crown is read as a shape rather than as a smudge.

props.note: No placements: Track I scatters it on the savanna horizon. Standing in for an acacia, which is a look choice. 5 m is the asset's own height. Poly Haven ships it at a density no browser needs for a tree seen from across the plateau, a 60 MB buffer that will not go under the 20 MB a file may be served at, so the finest level keeps a seventh of its faces.

props.name: Boulder
props.author: Poly Haven
props.attribution: "boulder_01" from Poly Haven, CC0 1.0. Decimated to three levels of detail and textured at 1024.
props.evidence: look choice: quarry rubble on the plateau
props.note: No placements: Track I scatters it. Sunk a quarter of a metre so it sits in the ground rather than on it, which is a look choice. 1.83 m is the asset's own length.
